I want to join SEEK because I deeply relate with its mission to inspire and mentor youth from underrepresented and low-income backgrounds in STEM fields. Growing up in a low-income family, I often had to teach myself advanced concepts while balancing work responsibilities. For example, I independently learned robotics, programming, and mechanics to co-found and lead my high school’s FTC robotics team. These experiences fixed in me the importance of perseverance and mentorship.
      As a QuestBridge Scholar, I have firsthand experience navigating the challenges that SEEK participants might face. QuestBridge's comprehensive approach, which recognizes academic achievement alongside personal resilience, gave me the opportunity to access higher education without financial barriers. Programs like QuestBridge and SEEK provide not only financial support but also mentorship and guidance, which can profoundly impact the trajectory of a student’s life. I want to give back by offering the same inspiration and support I received.
      Through my involvement with SHPE Jr. and other mentoring initiatives, I have seen how connecting with students can ignite their curiosity and confidence. I aim to use my STEM background, leadership skills, and personal experiences to empower SEEK participants to dream big and pursue careers in engineering. Joining SEEK aligns with my passion for mentorship and my goal to contribute meaningfully to my community while inspiring the next generation of engineers.

I’m really excited about the chance to join SEEK because it feels like the perfect fit for my passion for mentorship, community service, and education. I love the idea of working with kids and helping them explore STEM through hands-on projects. It’s inspiring to think about the impact we can have as mentors—not just teaching engineering concepts but also being positive role models for students who may not always have access to these opportunities.

As a Computer Class Teacher Assistant with the Refugee Promise Program, I taught computer literacy to adults, helped with resumes, and supported people as they learned new skills. It taught me patience, how to meet people where they’re at, and how rewarding it is to see someone gain confidence in themselves.

In my leadership roles with Best Buddies and Angelico House, I’ve worked on creating initiatives, planning events, and building communities. Whether it was raising awareness for individuals with intellectual disabilities or organizing service projects for my mentor group, I’ve always been driven by a desire to connect with people and make a difference.

SEEK’s mission really resonates with me because it’s not just about education—it’s about creating relationships and opening doors for kids who might not see themselves in STEM yet. I’d love to be part of a team that’s making such a tangible impact while also learning and growing alongside other mentors.

In high school, I worked as a math tutor at Mathnasium and developed a mini motor kit for younger students through the 'Shoulder of Giants'. Some preferred to learn visually while others were more analytical and everyone had their own pace. I learned how to adjust to each students' needs and developed a learning process that was fun for everyone. Through 'Shoulder of Giants', I worked with a professor to develop a unique, educational, and fun motor kit. We realized that many build it yourself motor kits on amazon or in stores oftentimes have missing parts, are complicated, don't explain the concepts behind the design, and have an underwhelming finished product. This can dissuade a kid dreaming of becoming an engineer so we wanted to design our own kit to solve these problems. We spent months doing research, designing our own motor on CAD, and building a prototype. We were able to showcase the prototype to some students where they were able to have fun building a motor, learn the principles behind it, and feel proud of completing a finished product. Being able to learn and explore the engineering process under a brilliant mentor and seeing kids happy faces was fulfilling and something I want to continue at UT SEEK.

For some background, during my junior year, I took the initiative to found a GirlUp Club at my school to create a safe space for young women from all different groups and cultures to come together and explore their academic passions, ranging from topics of engineering to business. Throughout my term as this club president, I led and mentored younger high school girls, encouraging them to pursue the topics that sparked their interests. Whether through our share circles, bracelet-making, or community service projects, I made it my goal to plan events that exposed members to inspiring mentors. My most profound belief in being a leader is that an astounding leader is a peer who always empowers those they lead. Thus, through the experience of uplifting these young students during my senior year of high school, I was able to be the best leader I could be, all while learning the remarkable stories of the girls I led. When asked about my experience with mentorship, my involvement as a cohort mentor for my local DECA chapter has provided me with opportunities to guide younger students. Through my role as a DECA mentor for my high school, I provided students with competition information and gave underclassmen meaningful advice. One of my freshmen mentees who asked me for advice, Ari, made a lasting impression on me with her eagerness to become more involved in DECA. Watching Ari’s hard work and dedication in coordination with my support as a mentor was one of the most rewarding experiences I’ve had. To me, being her mentor slowly shifted to more than just a role - it was a core experience. Lastly, my most prominent experience with outreach activities and events was my internship at CLEAN Cause, a local Austin energy drink company. During my time as an intern I contacted and created a database of the recovery homes and organizations that wanted to or had previously been working with CLEAN Cause. Through this project, I contacted over 1,000 organizations nationwide and shared the mission of CLEAN Cause, all while building vital relationships for the company, allowing me to partake in an outreach initiative. I truly believe my experience with leadership, mentorship, and outreach gives me a unique perspective on communication and an adaptable skill set I hope to bring to UT’s SEEK.
